title: The One Who…
description: Point at people and things by what they do: اللي 'who / that', ذاك اللي 'the one who', الشي اللي 'the thing that'. In a city where everybody knows everybody, this is how you say who you mean.
approach: GPA Phase 4 — the learner hears people identified by role and relation, then describes the people in their own life the same way.
unlock_condition: Identify three people from a picture using اللي clauses with a resumptive pronoun where needed
can_do: Describe people and things with 'who / that' clauses
Say 'the one that I…' with the pronoun that points back
Identify people by what they do and who they belong to

grammar.title: اللي after 'the', nothing after 'a'
grammar.explanation: When the noun has ال (or is a name or has a possessive ending), the description that follows is introduced by اللي: الرجّال اللي يشتغل مع عمك 'the man who works with your uncle'. When the noun is indefinite there is no اللي at all — رجّال يشتغل مع عمك 'a man who works with your uncle' is just two sentences run together. اللي never changes for gender or number: البنت اللي، الناس اللي. If the person or thing is the object inside the clause, put a pronoun back on the verb or preposition: البيت اللي سكنت فيه 'the house I lived in', الشخص اللي شفته 'the person I saw'. Never الذي / التي — nobody says them.

examples.arabic: الرجّال اللي يشتغل مع عمك أخوي
examples.transliteration: ir-rajjaal illi yishtaghil maʿ ʿammak akhuuy
examples.english: The man who works with your uncle is my brother
This is the driver who brought us yesterday

examples.arabic: البيت اللي سكنت فيه كان قديم
examples.transliteration: il-bayt illi sakant fiih kaan gadiim
examples.english: The house I lived in was old
I have a friend who knows the whole neighbourhood
The thing you said is right

culture.title: Who is he? The one whose uncle…
culture.note: In Yemen a person is placed by relation before by name: ولد عمي 'my cousin', اللي يشتغل مع خالك 'the one who works with your uncle', جماعة الحارة 'the neighbourhood folks'. Expect to be asked من أنت؟ and then من جماعتك؟ — which people are you from — and have an answer ready, even if it is 'the student who lives above the bakery'. When you describe someone, mention the tie that the listener shares: the mosque, the qat seller, the village. It is not gossip; it is how the map of the city is drawn. Asking about a woman by name is avoided — she is بنت فلان or أم فلان.

phrases.arabic: من هذا؟ — ذاك اللي يشتغل مع خالك
phrases.transliteration: man haadha? — dhaak illi yishtaghil maʿ khaalak
phrases.english: Who's that? — The one who works with your uncle
I'm the one who lives above the bakery

vocabulary.teaching_note: One word for who, that and which. Only after a definite noun. The most frequent Yemeni word after بس. Never الذي / التي.
vocabulary.image_scene: A crowd of people with one circled and an arrow to a caption box.

example.english: The girl who came yesterday is my sister

vocabulary.video_hint: Everywhere; اللي after any definite noun in narration.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'That one who': ذاك اللي يبيع القات 'the one who sells qat'. For a woman ذيك اللي, for people ذولاك اللي. هو اللي 'he's the one who' when you already named him.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man pointing across a market at a specific stall-holder.

example.english: The one who sells qat is my friend

vocabulary.video_hint: Someone pointed out in a crowd; ذاك اللي with the gesture.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'The thing that…': الشي اللي قلته 'what you said'. Also used for 'what I mean': الشي اللي أقصده. اللي alone can do this too.
vocabulary.image_scene: A hand pointing at a mystery box with a question mark on it.

example.arabic: الشي اللي يعجبني في صنعاء الجو
example.transliteration: ish-shi lli yiʿjibni fi ṣanʿaa j-jaww
example.english: The thing I like about Sanaa is the weather

vocabulary.video_hint: Reviews: 'the thing I liked was…' with الشي اللي.

vocabulary.teaching_note: شخص for a person in general; إنسان 'human being' when you praise — إنسان طيب 'a good soul'. Plural أشخاص. In speech واحد 'someone' does most of the work.
vocabulary.image_scene: A single silhouetted figure standing in a doorway.

example.english: This is the person I told you about

vocabulary.video_hint: Introductions; شخص / إنسان in a description of someone.

vocabulary.teaching_note: المكان اللي 'the place that…'. Plural أماكن. مكانك 'your seat / your place'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A map pin on a Sanaa rooftop café with mountains behind.

example.english: The place we had lunch in is nice

vocabulary.video_hint: Travel vlogs naming a spot; المكان اللي…

vocabulary.teaching_note: The spoken form of شيء — no hamza. كل شي 'everything', ما فيش شي 'nothing', شي حلو 'something nice'. Plural أشياء.
vocabulary.image_scene: A small wrapped parcel with a question mark tag.

example.english: Do you want anything from the market?

vocabulary.video_hint: Shopping and errand talk; تشتي شي؟

vocabulary.teaching_note: فيه أحد؟ 'is anyone there?'; ما فيش أحد 'there's nobody'. In fast Sanaa speech it shrinks to حد. Not the number.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man knocking on a door, calling in through a crack.

example.english: Is there anyone who knows the way?

vocabulary.video_hint: Someone calling into a house or room; فيه أحد؟

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Anyone whatsoever': أي حد يقدر 'anyone can'. أي واحد is the same. أي is the 'any / which' word.
vocabulary.image_scene: A row of different people all with a raised hand.
vocabulary.video_hint: Motivational or instructional clips; أي حد / أي واحد.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Everyone / all of them': الكل يعرفه 'everyone knows him'. كلنا 'all of us', كل الناس 'all the people'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A full mafraj, every face turned toward the camera.

example.english: Everyone in the neighbourhood knows each other

vocabulary.video_hint: Wedding and Eid gatherings; الكل / كلنا in the narration.

vocabulary.teaching_note: أي نوع؟ 'what kind?'. نوع القات، نوع الشغل. Plural أنواع.
vocabulary.image_scene: Three baskets of different qat bundles with labels.

example.english: What kind of qat do you want?

vocabulary.video_hint: Market clips comparing goods; نوع / أنواع.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Whoever / everyone who': كل من يجي 'whoever comes'. In relaxed speech اللي يجي says the same.
vocabulary.image_scene: An open door with a welcome mat and figures of all sizes walking in.

example.english: Whoever comes to the wedding eats

vocabulary.video_hint: Hospitality talk; كل من before a verb.

vocabulary.teaching_note: وين 'where' + ما = 'wherever': وين ما تسير 'wherever you go'. Same pattern as متى ما.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man with a backpack on a mountain path, arrows in all directions.

example.arabic: وين ما تسير في اليمن، تلقى كرم
example.transliteration: wayn maa tasiir fil-yaman, talga karam
example.english: Wherever you go in Yemen, you find generosity

vocabulary.teaching_note: Father's brother — and the respectful address for any older man: يا عم. عمي 'my uncle', ولد عمي 'my cousin'.
vocabulary.image_scene: An older man in a thawb and jambiya with a hand on a young man's shoulder.

example.english: My uncle, the one who works at the bank

vocabulary.video_hint: Family introductions; عمي / يا عم to an elder.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Mother's brother, the soft uncle in Yemeni family lore. خالي، خالك، أخوال. Aunt on that side is خالة.
vocabulary.image_scene: A smiling man handing sweets to children at a doorway.

example.english: That's my uncle, the one who has a shop

vocabulary.video_hint: Family vlogs; خالي introduced on camera.

vocabulary.teaching_note: ق is g. قريبي 'my relative', قرايب 'relatives'. The same word means 'near' — context decides.
vocabulary.image_scene: An extended family group photo on a rooftop.

example.english: He's my relative on my mother's side

vocabulary.video_hint: Wedding vlogs: 'all the relatives came' — قرايب.

vocabulary.teaching_note: الناس اللي 'the people who'. ناس طيبين 'good people'. No singular — that is شخص.
vocabulary.image_scene: A busy Old Sanaa lane with people of all ages.

example.english: The people here are all kind

vocabulary.video_hint: Street scenes; الناس in the description.

vocabulary.teaching_note: معروف في الحارة 'known in the neighbourhood'. Also 'a favour': اعمل لي معروف 'do me a favour'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A shopkeeper greeted by everyone passing his stall.

example.arabic: هذا الدكتور معروف في صنعاء كلها
example.transliteration: haadha d-duktoor maʿruuf fi ṣanʿaa kullaha
example.english: This doctor is well-known in all of Sanaa

vocabulary.video_hint: Descriptions of a famous local; معروف / مشهور.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Your people': جماعتك means your family and circle. يا جماعة 'hey everyone'. جماعة الحارة 'the neighbourhood crowd'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A cluster of men in futas chatting outside a mosque.
vocabulary.video_hint: Addresses to a crowd — يا جماعة — in vlogs and sketches.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: من هذا اللي يسلّم على الكل؟
dialogue.transliteration: man haadha lli ysallim ʿala l-kull?

dialogue.speaker: Salem
dialogue.arabic: ذاك اللي يشتغل مع خالك في البنك
dialogue.transliteration: dhaak illi yishtaghil maʿ khaalak fil-bank
dialogue.english: The one who works with your uncle at the bank

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: آه، الشخص اللي حكيت لي عنه؟
dialogue.transliteration: aah, ish-shakhṣ illi ḥakiit li ʿannuh?
dialogue.english: Ah, the person you told me about?

dialogue.speaker: Salem
dialogue.arabic: إي، هو قريبنا. معروف في الحارة كلها
dialogue.transliteration: ii, huu gariibna. maʿruuf fil-ḥaara kullaha
dialogue.english: Yes, he's our relative. Well-known in the whole neighbourhood

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: الشي اللي يعجبني فيه إنه يعرف كل الناس
dialogue.transliteration: ish-shi lli yiʿjibni fiih innuh yiʿrif kull in-naas
dialogue.english: The thing I like about him is that he knows everybody

dialogue.speaker: Salem
dialogue.arabic: كل من يعرفه يحبه. تعال نسلّم عليه
dialogue.transliteration: kull man yiʿrifuh yiḥibbuh. taʿaal nsallim ʿalayh
dialogue.english: Whoever knows him loves him. Come, let's go and greet him

sound_spotlight.example: الشي اللي (ish-shi lli)، هو اللي (huu lli)
sound_spotlight.explanation: After a word ending in a vowel, اللي loses its first vowel and becomes lli — the two words fuse. Listen for the doubled l, not a separate word.
The -h on فيه is short and unstressed but it is what makes the sentence complete. Leaving it out sounds like English word order pasted onto Arabic.
gariib is both 'near' and 'relative' — same word, same hard g. Only context tells you which.

lesson_sequence.detail: The Ali–Salem dialogue once; the learner picks the man being described from four faces.
Ten pairs of sentences (البيت اللي… / بيت …); the learner hears them and taps whether اللي was present and why.
The 18 words with images; the family words (عم، خال، قريب، جماعة) grouped as the relation set.
Fill-the-gap with the resumptive pronoun: البيت اللي سكنت ___، الشخص اللي شفت___.
A picture of a street with six people; the app names roles and the learner identifies each with ذاك اللي…
Record three sentences describing people in your life with اللي and a relation word.
Counter; nudge to ask من جماعتك؟ style questions politely.
